title: Agent-Canary-Mas: End-to-End Evaluation of Protocol Risk in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Systems
abstract: arXiv:2610.15529v2 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent-to-agent protocols allow LLM agents to discover peers, exchange results, and coordinate tool use. A locally successful protocol attack, however, may be rejected by a later agent or propagated into a consequential task decision. Measuring local exploitability alone leaves this difference unresolved and provides limited evidence about which participant caused the final outcome.   We present Agent-Canary-Mas, an end-to-end evaluation system that follows protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks. It covers five risk classes and 13 subclasses across A2A, ANP, and BCS, with 975 matched malicious--benign task pairs in five business domains. A shared OpenClaw framework runs autonomous, tool-using agents under different underlying models while preserving the task and execution setup. translated_title: Agent-Canary-Mas：长时程多智能体系统中协议风险的端到端评估
translated_abstract: 智能体间协议使LLM智能体能够发现对等体、交换结果并协调工具使用。然而，一个在本地成功的协议攻击可能被后续智能体拒绝，也可能传播为影响重大的任务决策。仅测量本地可利用性无法解决这一差异，也难以提供关于哪个参与者导致了最终结果的证据。我们提出了Agent-Canary-Mas，这是一个端到端评估系统，用于追踪长时程多智能体任务中的协议风险。它涵盖了A2A、ANP和BCS三种协议下的五个风险类别和13个子类，在五个业务领域中包含975对匹配的恶意-良性任务对。共享的OpenClaw框架在不同底层模型下运行自主的、可使用工具的智能体，同时保持任务和执行设置的一致性。匹配运行将本地协议成功与下游后果分离开来；保留的证据将参与者选择、消息消费与最终任务结果联系起来。
tldr: 提出了端到端评估系统Agent-Canary-Mas，通过覆盖三大协议、975对匹配的恶意-良性任务对，将本地协议攻击的可利用性与长时程多智能体任务中的下游实际后果区分开来，并追溯最终结果的归因。
en_tdlr: Agent-Canary-Mas is an end-to-end evaluation system that traces protocol risk through long-horizon multi-agent tasks across 975 matched malicious-benign pairs, separating local protocol exploitability from downstream consequences and attributing final outcomes to responsible participants.
